readings.subject: Selected control: whether the retained circular triggers complex-product treatment for distribution of a particular Fund
readings.statement: [TRUE_IS_SATISFIED] For an SFC-authorised fund offered to the public in Hong Kong that is not a listed closed-ended alternative asset fund, the classification trigger is satisfied when its aggregate direct and indirect exposure to private market assets is at least 50% of NAV, or when the SFC has actually designated it as a complex product on a case-by-case basis. True means that this circular supplies a basis requiring complex-product treatment for distribution. False, within scope and with the relevant facts established, means that neither classification route is established under this selected control; it does not establish non-complex status under every other applicable rule. Missing exposure or designation evidence remains unknown. The retained text supports one classification structure; the principal unresolved issues concern exposure measurement, timing and evidence, rather than a competing rule making every private-market exposure automatically complex.
readings.distinction: The threshold sentence uses mandatory language, while the below-threshold route requires an SFC designation and permits a holistic assessment. For example, an in-scope Fund with established aggregate exposure of exactly 50% satisfies the trigger without a separate designation. A Fund at 49% with established absence of an SFC designation does not satisfy this selected trigger merely because its CLO holdings or liquidity profile warrant scrutiny; a Fund at 49% that has actually been designated does satisfy it. An otherwise comparable LAF falls outside this circular's defined Fund scope. A Fund whose exposure or designation history is missing cannot be treated as the established 49%-and-undesignated case. Footnote 7 supports attaching holistic assessment to cases below 50%, rather than making the express 50% threshold discretionary. The strongest uncertainty is how to establish aggregate exposure for layered instruments and the relevant assessment date.

citations.quote: This circular provides guidance to management companies of funds that are authorised by the SFC for offering to the public in Hong Kong (Funds)6 in this regard.
Except for listed closed-ended alternative asset funds (LAFs).
A Fund will be considered as a complex product if its total direct and indirect exposures to private market assets amount to 50% or more of the Fund’s NAV.
On a case-by-case basis, the SFC may also designate a Fund as a complex product, taking into account factors including, without limitation:
In assessing whether the complex product designation is warranted7, the SFC will adopt a holistic approach taking into account the specific circumstances of the case.
In cases where the Fund’s aggregate direct and indirect exposures to private market assets are less than 50% of the Fund’s NAV.

A Fund classified as a complex product will be subject to the SFC’s prevailing requirements for the sale of complex products8 including but not limited to ensuring the suitability of the Fund for its investors irrespective of whether solicitation or recommendation is involved.
Fund managers are encouraged to consult the SFC at the earliest opportunity if they are in doubt regarding complex product classification of their Funds.

assumptions: The formalization evaluates one particular fund at one identified assessment time; it does not determine whole-firm compliance or satisfaction of the downstream sales requirements.
Footnote 6 qualifies the defined population of Funds, and footnote 7 qualifies the holistic designation assessment in cases below 50%.
The designation fact records an actual, applicable SFC designation. A manager's view that designation is likely or appropriate does not establish that fact.
The threshold fact must be established using a supportable exposure measurement. The formalization supplies no missing valuation, look-through, aggregation or monitoring convention.

A result is interpreted only within the Boolean scope. Unknown facts are not assigned false values; one established true classification route can nevertheless establish the result without resolving the other route.
questions: How should indirect exposure through BDCs, CLOs, TRSs and SRTs be measured and aggregated, including look-through, derivative exposure and possible double counting?
What valuation date, monitoring frequency and treatment of temporary threshold crossings govern the 50% test?
What evidence establishes an applicable SFC designation, its effective date and any subsequent withdrawal or replacement?
Does omitted commencement or transitional material specify when existing Funds must complete classification changes and distributor communications?

facts.name: sfc_authorised_public_fund
facts.meaning: Whether the particular fund is authorised by the SFC for offering to the public in Hong Kong at the assessment time.

facts.name: listed_closed_ended_alternative_asset_fund
facts.meaning: Whether the particular fund falls within the listed closed-ended alternative asset fund category excluded by footnote 6. An unresolved category classification remains unknown.

facts.name: aggregate_private_market_exposure_at_least_half_nav
facts.meaning: Whether established total direct and indirect exposure to private market assets amounts to at least 50% of the Fund's NAV at the assessment time. Supplying this fact requires resolving applicable exposure measurement and aggregation; missing holdings or measurement evidence is not false.

facts.name: applicable_sfc_complex_product_designation
facts.meaning: Whether an actual SFC case-by-case designation of the particular Fund as a complex product applies at the assessment time. Mere risk factors, possible designation or an unsearched designation history do not establish a positive or negative value.

dimensions.explanation: The defined Funds are authorised for public offering in Hong Kong, with LAFs excluded. Guidance is addressed to management companies and fund managers; designation is an SFC decision and attaches to the Fund. Distribution consequences include suitability requirements, while managers must select suitably knowledgeable distributors. Scrutiny of new authorisation applications is a separate process and does not itself establish complex-product classification.

Private market assets collectively cover private credit and private equity. Direct and indirect routes and instrument examples are supplied, and the indirect list is expressly non-exhaustive. The inclusive threshold is clear, but the retained text does not settle how fund-level holdings translate into measured underlying exposure, derivative exposure or netting. These are unresolved measurement questions, not authority to select a convenient convention. The separate 15% direct-investment limit is not the complex-product threshold and does not remove direct exposure from aggregation.

Footnote 6 excludes LAFs from the defined Fund population; it does not establish that LAFs are non-complex under their separate regime. Footnote 7 locates holistic designation assessment below 50%, rather than creating a waiver above the mandatory threshold. Exposure below 50% is therefore not a blanket exemption. The sales consequence expressly applies irrespective of solicitation or recommendation.

The threshold entails classification; the SFC may additionally designate individual Funds below it through holistic assessment. Aggregate exposure, strategy, portfolio, liquidity, risk, instrument characteristics and home-regulator conditions inform that discretion without becoming independent automatic classification triggers. Enhanced disclosure is separately required. Review expectations and encouraged consultation do not turn classification into an optional manager decision or make missing evidence an exemption.

The packet distinguishes new applications from existing Funds and expects appropriate action, including offering-document updates as soon as practicable. It supplies no calendar commencement date, fixed transition deadline, exposure observation convention or reclassification rule. The dates 30 April 2014, 4 March 2016 and April 2013 describe referenced materials, not this circular's commencement. The instruction to apply prevailing sales requirements and the possibility of updating exposure examples introduce temporal dependencies that the retained text alone cannot resolve.

Referenced but unprovided materials include UT Code section 7.3, the LAF circular, Code of Conduct paragraph 5.5, Online Distribution and Advisory Platforms Guidelines chapter 6, relevant FAQs, product-approval guidance and advertising guidelines. They prevent a complete account of downstream distribution obligations and the excluded LAF regime. The packet also lists three unresolved dependency identifiers without contents or a mapping to particular references; their substance cannot be inferred. Classification additionally depends on fund-specific holdings, measurement evidence and applicable SFC decisions. The reference to paragraphs 9 and 10 cannot be mapped conclusively from the supplied unit locators alone.

coverage.reason: Defines private market assets and identifies direct and indirect exposure routes relevant to aggregation.
Establishes the Fund and manager scope and distinguishes disclosure requirements from possible scrutiny and classification.
Explains the risk rationale for scrutiny; the described risks are not independent automatic classification triggers.
States disclosure and distributor-selection expectations surrounding the selected classification control.
Heading identifies the separate enhanced-disclosure section.
Potential exposure triggers offering-document disclosure; that trigger is broader than mandatory complex-product classification.
Exposure-disclosure examples help identify relevant evidence but supply no binding aggregation methodology.
Underlying-asset disclosures can inform assessment of indirect exposures without determining classification themselves.
Specific risk disclosures are a separate obligation and contextual evidence for the Fund's risk characteristics.
Heading identifies the classification section.
Supplies the inclusive mandatory 50% threshold and the additional case-by-case designation route.
Aggregate exposure also informs discretionary designation below the automatic threshold.
Strategy, composition, liquidity and risk are discretionary assessment factors, not standalone automatic triggers.
Instrument characteristics inform designation; the examples do not classify every CLO or SRT holding automatically.
Home-regulator conditions are relevant discretionary factors; no automatic substitution for an SFC designation is stated.
Requires holistic assessment for the designation cases qualified by footnote 7.
Connects classification to prevailing complex-product sales requirements, including suitability without solicitation or recommendation.
Heading introduces target-market and distributor-selection obligations.
Incorporates separate product-approval guidance; its full obligations are outside the selected classification predicate.
Managers must select distributors capable of understanding classification and assigning an appropriate risk rating; risk rating is not equated with complex-product designation.
Advertising requirements remain separate from the selected classification trigger.
Section heading has no independent classification condition.
Possible enhanced scrutiny and exclusion from FASTrack for new applications do not themselves establish complex-product status.
Existing Funds require review, appropriate action and distributor communication; consultation is encouraged when classification is uncertain, without a specified calendar deadline.
Identifies a clarification channel rather than a classification condition.
Identifies the issuing division without adding a substantive rule.
Identifies the named institution in the retained source; no independent authenticity determination is made.
The separate 15% direct-investment limit neither replaces the aggregate 50% classification threshold nor excludes direct investments from it.
Prevents treating listed indirect-exposure examples as exhaustive and identifies possible future updates.
Provides the retained BDC description but does not specify the amount of a holding counted as private-market exposure.
Describes CLO collateral, informing exposure identification without resolving tranche-level measurement.
Identifies TRS and SRT examples; derivative exposure measurement remains unspecified.
Excludes LAFs from this circular's Fund scope and refers their treatment to a separate unprovided circular.
Attaches the below-50% qualification to holistic designation assessment.
Identifies sources governing downstream sales requirements; their unprovided contents cannot be reconstructed from this citation.
Dates the referenced product-approval guidance; those dates do not establish commencement of the retained circular.
Identifies and dates the referenced advertising guidelines as described by the source; their contents and current version are not independently established.
